title: AI Debt Has Exploded 4X To Nearly $500 Billion: What It Means For NVDA, ORCL And CRWV, According To IO Fund - Stocktwits
content: Artificial intelligence is becoming a financeable infrastructure asset class as companies increasingly turn to debt markets to fund data centers and AI hardware, according to IO Fund. Morgan Stanley data cited by IO Fund shows AI-related debt issuance reached $466 billion through September, up from $101 billion during the same period in 2025. Goldman Sachs puts the figure at $489 billion as of July 22, already above the $322 billion raised throughout 2025. Nvidia shares closed 0.6% lower on Friday, Oracle shares closed 0.5% higher, while CoreWeave shares fell more than 2%. IO Fund's analysis shows Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Oracle Corp. (ORCL) and CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) occupy different positions in the debt-funded AI infrastructure chain. Lenders fund borrowers such as Oracle, CoreWeave and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX), which use that financing to purchase chips from suppliers including Nvidia. The borrowers then rent compute capacity to customers, while suppliers collect payment when chips are delivered. For Nvidia, the financing surge is supporting chip purchases across the ecosystem, analysts at IO Fund said. Nvidia generated $127 billion in free cash flow over the 12 months ended July 2026, IO Fund noted. It also added that Nvidia has signed preliminary agreements with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR targeting more than $500 billion in third-party capital. CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia retains the option to backstop up to $125 billion across these structures. IO Fund also notes that borrowers pay Nvidia and other chip suppliers upfront while customer revenue arrives over multi-year contracts. “AI compute is becoming a financeable infrastructure asset class,” IO Fund said. For Oracle, the debt burden is already visible in its financials, IO Fund stated, while adding that Oracle reported $125.3 billion in notes payable and borrowings in the first quarter (Q1). This is over three times its $37.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. Quarterly interest expense rose 55% year over year to $1.43 billion. Oracle also has $288 billion of new data center leases that have not yet started, with terms of 15 to 19 years. IO Fund said Oracle is reportedly considering an investor-funded entity that would purchase chips and lease them to the company, keeping the debt with the separate entity until the leases begin. For CoreWeave, IO Fund's analysis points to the direct cost of financing rapid capacity expansion. The neocloud generated $2.6 billion in second-quarter (Q2) revenue while spending $9.4 billion on quarterly capex, most of which was financed by debt. CoreWeave's total debt reached about $35.6 billion, while FY2026 capex guidance increased to $35 billion-$39 billion. Its Q2 interest expense jumped 140% year over year to $640 million, and the company guided to $860 million-$940 million for the third quarter (Q3). “That means more than 25% of its revenue goes to servicing its debt,” IO Fund wrote. CoreWeave also has approximately $15 billion of total debt due through 2028, while some higher-interest debt carrying rates above 10% is due in 2030 and beyond. IO Fund also highlighted 14 circular financing arrangements identified by the IMF across the broader GPU ecosystem, linking lenders, chip suppliers, infrastructure operators and AI customers. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Nvidia trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing. NVDA stock is up 13% year-to-date, ORCL stock is down 35%, while CRWV stock is down 24%. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 15% over the past 12 months, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) is up 25%. Bitcoin's (BTC) price edged lower on Sunday as long-term gold advocate Peter Schiff warned that the apex cryptocurrency was "finally breaking down," with "the next stop" likely at $75,000. After Bitcoin dipped below $80,000, Schiff said, "It's hard to believe it's held up this long.” He explained that if the $75,000 level failed to hold, "it's going to be a very long weekend for Bitcoiners, especially for ETF investors who can't sell until Monday." Spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) trade only when US stock markets are open, while Bitcoin trades around the clock. The weekend dip followed two straight days of selling in those funds. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a total of $773.5 million in net outflows on Thursday and Friday, according to Farside Investors data. Bitcoin’s price traded around $80,166, down 0.3% over 24 hours, after briefly falling to the $79,000 range. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ over the past day. Additionally, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which tracks market mood, sat at 40, in "Fear" territory. Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone also struck a cautious tone. He said "Don't fight the Fed" may be "the look-back lesson of 4Q," especially for what he called "high-beta, volatile, correlated stock puppets like Bitcoin (cryptos), and gold, copper (metals)." McGlone said the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) "trades about 3x the volatility" of the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT). He added that the ratio between the two "appears to be rolling over" from a base set at the end of 2024. According to him, a recent flush of "leveraged longs in US Treasury bonds and shorts in Bitcoin" might be "the foundation for a potential move of a lifetime that is simple mean reversion." It is important to note that McGlone has called for Bitcoin’s slide toward $10,000 before. In July, he said the cryptocurrency was in a "severe, serious bear market" that was "just getting started." Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. “The Big Short” investor Michael Burry drew comparisons between the current stock market and the dot-com era, calling the current market “uncannily close” to 2000, while adding that the S&P 500’s internal breadth looks unusually weak even as the index remains near record highs. In his latest Substack note, Burry analyzed stocks that have fallen sharply from their highs, asking whether the market’s biggest laggards could become the unexpected winners if today’s bull market eventually gives way to a bear market. Burry split the S&P 500 into three groups, namely, “Leaders,” “Broken stocks,” and “Busted stocks”. Burry defined “Leaders” as stocks which are within 10% of their 10-year highs. “Broken stocks” are those which are down 20%-40% from these highs, while “Busted stocks” are those which are down more than 40%. “The Big Short” investor noted that the current setup closely resembles the months surrounding the March 2000 market top. He highlighted that as of the Oct. 6 record high, 23% of S&P 500 stocks were already Busted, with the median Busted stock down 55% from its high. In 2000, 32% were Busted, with a median decline of 52%. However, Burry said the bigger warning comes from the leadership itself. Just 15 S&P 500 stocks closed at record highs on Oct. 6, while only 97 were within 10% of their highs, which is strikingly similar to the numbers during the March 2000 peak. More importantly, 58% of today's Leaders were already 5%-10% below their highs, which Burry describes as unusually “soft” leadership. “It is striking,” Burry added. He found that the Oct. 6 record was at or beyond the 95th percentile on all seven of his key market-top measures, which is a combination he says has appeared only during the final months leading into the 2000 peak. Burry examined what happened to beaten-down stocks after previous market tops, saying that the March 2000 peak was the standout. He highlighted that eighteen months after that top, Busted stocks gained 18% on a median basis, while Leaders plunged 50%. At 12 months, Busted stocks were up 19%, compared with a 33% decline for Leaders. Burry said that this makes the current cohort of deeply beaten-down stocks particularly interesting, while adding that simply being down 40% does not make a stock cheap. Instead, Burry says he looks at owners’ earnings, return on invested capital and valuation. Among the Busted stocks, he highlights names including Lululemon Athletica Inc. (LULU), PayPal Holdings Inc. (PYPL), Fiserv Inc. (FISV), Deckers Outdoor Corp. (DEC), Zoetis Inc. (ZTS) and Adobe Inc. (ADBE) as examples of companies that combine relatively strong business characteristics with depressed valuations. He also points to AppLovin Corp. (APP), which has one of the highest calculated ROIC figures among the Busted group even after his adjustment for stock-based compensation. “This is not shooting fish in a barrel,” Burry cautioned. Burry's comparison between 2000 and 2026 also leads him toward smaller companies. He argues that today's Busted stocks are not as cheap as their counterparts were in 2000. The median price-to-earnings ratio for today's Busted stocks is about 17.2 times, versus 10.2 times in 2000. Median price-to-sales is also substantially higher today. That could limit how much capital simply rotates from today's market leaders into beaten-down S&P 500 stocks. Instead, Burry sees the possibility of money moving outside the index — particularly into smaller companies and small-cap value. He points to the period from 1999 through 2007, when the Russell 2000 Small Cap Value Total Return Index substantially benefited as liquidity moved away from large-cap leaders. Today, he says he has found enough opportunities among Busted stocks, international equities and small-cap value to remain essentially fully invested alongside his short positions. “Time will tell if this is as it appears - a 2000 redux, with the Busted far outperforming the Leaders - or just another bear market where the Busted fall along with the Leaders,” Burry said. During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.15%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.07%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.13%. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Elon Musk on Saturday said Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) restricted Ukraine’s access to Starlink after the country’s military violated the service’s terms by using the civilian satellite network for offensive drone strikes. Musk said in a post on X that Starlink remains critical to Ukraine’s defense, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that Starlink and Starshield operations had returned to their previous speeds. SpaceX shares gained nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading session, and edged up by 0.1% further during the afterhours trade. Musk said Starlink was never intended to be used for offensive operations involving attacks on people, arguing that Ukraine’s military had violated the service’s terms of service. “Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he added. He also distinguished Starlink from Starshield, saying the latter is a separate system controlled by the U.S. government, while noting that what the administration decides to do with it is up to them. Musk added that Ukraine’s use of Starlink for offensive drone strikes was done by exploiting a loophole that SpaceX moved to close last week. Despite the restrictions, Musk said Starlink remains essential to Ukraine’s military because he believes it is currently the only communications system that cannot be jammed or destroyed. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” he said. Musk also pointed to Starlink’s role during the early stages of Russia’s invasion, saying Russian attacks had destroyed or jammed other communications systems. “SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth by far,” he said. Zelenskyy confirmed in a post on X on Saturday that Starlink and Starshield operations had been restored to the speeds Ukraine had before the restrictions, saying the improvement began overnight and was already sufficient by Sunday morning. “The most important thing today is that Starlink and Starshield operations have been restored to the speeds we had before the restrictions,” he said. Zelenskyy added that the restoration was important for Ukraine’s frontline operations, including logistics and defense against Russian drones with jet-powered “shaheds.” Zelenskyy also thanked U.S. officials and others who he said helped address the issue, including members of Congress, senators, the State Department and the president. The latest dispute comes after a report stated that both the Biden and Trump administrations had repeatedly asked SpaceX to adjust Starlink access in Ukraine and the Middle East. The report said U.S. officials had asked SpaceX to expand availability in Ukraine and Iran while restricting access for Iran-backed groups in the Middle East. Amid this, Trump said on Friday that he believed the issue had been fixed and defended Musk, calling him a “very brilliant person” and saying, “Elon will never do anything wrong.” Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around SpaceX trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing. Hyperliquid (HYPE) edged lower on Saturday, even after its treasury company, Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), more than tripled its stock buyback program to $100 million. Hyperliquid Strategies said on Friday that its board approved raising its stock repurchase program from $30 million to up to $100 million. About $72 million remained available under the expanded authorization, which meant that the company had already used roughly $28 million. The program's end date also moved from December 5, 2026, to October 31, 2027. The company said the increase reflected the “Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy." Hyperliquid Strategies is "currently the largest HYPE-focused digital asset treasury vehicle." Among the risks it listed in its announcement, it said its stock price "will be highly correlated to the price of HYPE tokens." Hyperliquid Strategies held about 38.8 million HYPE tokens, worth roughly $2.9 billion, according to its treasury dashboard. PURR stock closed up over 1% on Friday. Bitcoin (BTC) fell to $80,000 on Saturday as traditional financial assets including stocks, ETFs, indices, gold and oil are capturing a larger share of trading activity on crypto exchanges. Perpetual futures tied to these assets made up 23.5% of volume in August, up from just 0.5% in November of last year, according to a report by Glassnode and Fasanara Digital. Perpetual futures are derivatives with no expiry date, which allow traders to hold leveraged positions for as long as they like. The share of these contracts tied to traditional assets rose from 0.5% of volume on six major exchange groups in November 2025 to 23.5% in August 2026, the report said. About $778 billion worth changed hands in August alone, up from $23.5 billion in November. Trading in crypto-asset perpetuals fell 49% over the same period, which also lifted the traditional-asset share. Even if crypto volume had stayed at its November level, the share would still have reached 13.5% in August, the report said. The firms noted that their figures are conservative. Contracts they could not classify were counted as crypto. Bitcoin was the top-trending ticker on Stocktwits. Bitcoin’s price was down over 2% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day. Binance (BNB) did not list its first such contract until December 2025. By August, it handled about 55% of the volume, or $429 billion. OKX came second with a little over 15%, followed by Hyperliquid (HYPE) at 11%. Traditional assets made up a larger part of the business on Hyperliquid, as they accounted for 35.2% of all perpetual volume on the platform in August, against 27.6% on Binance. Hyperliquid’s (HYPE) HIP-3 system, live since October 2025, allows users to create perpetual markets for any asset that has a reliable price source. Markets listed on trade.xyz, an exchange built on that system, now trade 85% as much volume as Hyperliquid’s own Bitcoin perpetual, up from less than a tenth at the start of the year, the report said. At the start of the year, it was below a tenth. The same types of contracts topped the rankings on every platform. These included memory-chip stocks, leveraged chip and Korea-focused ETFs, and commodities such as gold, silver and crude oil. The report also tracked Bitcoin's behavior around the U.S. Treasury's decision to raise the maximum size of its long-dated bond buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Bitcoin rose 25% that week, while gold climbed and stocks slipped. Since then, Bitcoin has traded more like gold. Their correlation peaked on September 11 at its highest level since the data began in March 2018, according to the report. title: Nvidia’s New $3 Billion AI Bet Is on One of Its Own Customers - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia’s $3 billion investment in Meta strengthens an important partnership. It also raises familiar questions about who is funding the AI boom. Nvidia (NVDA +0.90%) announced this morning that it plans to invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms (META -1.65%), one of its biggest customers. Nvidia will make the investment as part of Meta's recently announced stock offering. The companies said they will expand their work on Muse, Meta's popular AI assistant, working to improve Meta's family of models that power it. That technical partnership aims to improve both training -- building an AI model -- and inference, using the model after it's been trained. Meta said it plans to expand its deployment of Nvidia's latest hardware: Vera Rubin GPU systems, Vera CPUs, and networking technology. The companies also said they are considering working on tools that would help AI agents operate securely as well as help monitor their behavior, but those discussions are still exploratory and nothing has been agreed upon. This is a deepening of an already close relationship. While we don't know where exactly Meta ranks, it was very likely already one of Nvidia's biggest customers, and in February, Meta said it would deploy millions of Nvidia's Blackwell and Vera Rubin GPUs, along with CPUs and networking equipment. And given the lack of detail in this announcement, it makes it a little hard to tell how much new business Nvidia is actually getting here. Meta says it will use more of its hardware, but the announcement doesn't say how much more or what those additional purchases will be worth. And their engineers were already working together, so the technical partnership sounds like an extension of work they were already doing. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » More than three years into the AI boom, Nvidia is still going strong. Last quarter, the company's top-line reached $96.2 billion, more than double what it recorded a year earlier. Operating profit grew a whopping 124% to $63.7 billion. It's easy to take this for granted at this point, but those really are simply incredible growth numbers for a company of this size. Unsurprisingly, Nvidia's data center business accounted for more than 90% of sales. While that is precisely what's fueling the company's rapid growth, it means Nvidia's fate is directly tied to the rest of the AI industry. Nvidia -- or rather, its stock price -- cannot afford to have the AI capex spend slow. The deal made today makes sense. Meta needs capital, and Nvidia is flush with cash. A $3 billion infusion gives Nvidia an appreciating asset -- Meta stock -- while ensuring a major customer continues to purchase its hardware. This is one of many such deals that, while completely above-board, have raised concerns over whether Nvidia is using its considerable balance sheet to paper over cracks in a less-than-healthy AI ecosystem. I think there's something to these claims, though I would caution investors to read too much into a deal like this. The reality is, Nvidia has a whole lot of cash on hand and needs to do something with it. Meta stock is a reasonable place to deploy that capital. That said, given the recent issues that hyperscalers like Meta -- and especially neoclouds like CoreWeave -- have been facing related to debt financing, it's reasonable to question how sustainable the AI buildout really is at this point. title: Nvidia (NVDA) & AMD to invest combined $4 billion into Facebook (META) - Shacknews
content: Both AMD and Nvidia want to deepen their ties with Meta's Muse family of AI models as Meta seeks to raise $95 billion in investments to support its AI infrastructure. Graphics, processing, and AI tech giants Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD have announced a combined $4 billion of investments into Facebook (META) with $3 billion coming from Nvidia. This will go into a round of funding in which Meta is hoping to gather a reported $95 billion in support of its AI technologies. Nvidia and AMD announced their investments into Meta in separate press releases. The hardware of both Nvidia and AMD are used to power Meta's Muse AI models, which the two both express as a major factor in the investment. These investments will also support future tech collaborations between Meta and the two companies. “NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in his company’s statement. AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su also expressed enthusiasm for the company’s growing partnership with Meta: With Helios now running at Meta, we are taking that partnership to a new scale in the superintelligence era. Together, we are building and deploying infrastructure at gigawatt scale and shaping future generations of silicon, software and systems to enable Meta’s most ambitious superintelligence models and services. Meta had another solid quarter in its Q3 2026 earnings, clearing over $64 billion in revenue. It remains one of the biggest developers of AI models in the world and the craze shows no sign of stopping as companies continue to spend billions on growth and infrastructure. With its investment round continuing, and AMD and Nvidia on board, stay tuned to the Meta topic for more news and updates. Separately, Meta increased the size of its common stock offering from $22.5 billion to $25 billion, bringing the combined potential proceeds from its common stock and depository share offerings to $37.5 billion. Under the expanded partnership, Nvidia and Meta will work together to improve the performance of Meta's Muse artificial intelligence models, including the computing processes used for model training and inference. The memory chip industry has long been cyclical because it's a commodity business in which it is difficult for the manufacturers to keep supply and demand balanced. For decades, new technologies and devices would periodically appear that led to surges in demand and rising chip prices. Chipmakers would then collectively build out production capacity -- a process that takes a couple of years -- only to overshoot as a group, leading to an excess of supply. Recently, memory stocks have once again come under pressure as investors worry about new competition in the space and signs that future demand may not be as ironclad as the market thinks. However, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that he isn't worried that memory demand will slacken even by 2029, which is a longer time horizon than most analysts have speculated on thus far. Does Huang know something Wall Street doesn't? Memory, including NAND flash memory and dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), has become deeply supply-constrained as GPU clusters and data centers have scaled, creating unheard-of levels of demand. Memory supply is so constrained that several consumer electronics companies have announced price hikes on products due specifically to higher memory prices. As such, the memory stocks mentioned above have soared this year. Micron is up roughly 172%, Samsung is up 66%, and SK Hynix has risen roughly 81%. This has led much of the industry to conclude that memory will be supply-constrained until sometime next year, or even into 2028. This thesis was recently put to the test when the Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced it would roll out a new memory architecture by year-end that could pack more memory cells into the same amount of space. CNBC also reported that a well-known South Korean publication, citing Professor Hwang Cheol-seong, a distinguished professor of materials science and engineering at Seoul National University, and Ahn Ki-hyun, executive director of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association, published an article that said the two expect a "flood of new [memory] supply" that will create a "red ocean" in 2019. These comments naturally led to a big sell-off in the memory space. But on Oct. 22, Huang told CNBC that he doesn't foresee a memory glut by 2029 as his base case. "One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang told CNBC at a recent conference in Berlin. Huang also said Nvidia is open to working with a company like CXMT. Wall Street has been anxious in recent months, and the latest spate of news items has been crushing memory stocks. Although Huang tends to be a perma-bull on artificial intelligence, aside from the ChangXin news and the South Korean article, there is no evidence that demand is slowing. For instance, Micron and SK Hynix have signed numerous three- to five-year deals with some of their largest customers that lock in price ranges and sales volumes. This cyclical sector has not seen such longer-term contracts before. Meanwhile, SK Hynix has said it plans to triple its wafer capacity by 2034 to meet the incredible demand it's seeing. Counterpoint Research actually forecasts that DRAM prices will fall by 23% in 2028 compared to 2027. However, even after that decline, they would still be 230% higher than levels seen in 2025. "The current memory market is considered to be in a 'New Normal' era, and the down cycle will differ from previous ones," Counterpoint senior research analyst Jeongku Choi told CNBC. This recent rout in memory stocks shows how touchy the market is. As with everything in AI, memory prices don't show any sign of coming down, but the slightest hint that they could begin to retreat to their pre-AI supercycle levels would certainly send the stocks tumbling. That's why I'd still recommend investors not go too heavy on their exposure to this group. I think it's certainly OK to have some portfolio exposure because the AI trade could still be a long-term winner, but this sector will be volatile, and it will be quite difficult to get ahead of the memory cycle. title: Nvidia Picks Up $3B Stock In Meta's Equity Offering, Will Help Improve Muse AI Platform - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp (NVDA) said early Tuesday that it is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms’ (META) equity offering and will partner with the social media giant to improve its Muse AI agentic platform. Meta announced a massive $97.5 billion equity offering on Monday and said later in the day that it sold $12.5 billion of preferred shares at $50 apiece and $25 billion of common stock at $625 per share. The offer includes about $60 billion in an at-the-market share sale program, including the company’s planned Class C nonvoting shares. Meta said earlier that Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO) had agreed to buy as much as $5 billion of the common shares in aggregate. Meta intends to use the proceeds to support its investment in AI infrastructure and its consumer AI tools. NVDA stock was down 0.6% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday, while META shares were flat. Large-cap tech names were mixed following Anthropic’s IPO filing, although some memory stocks eked out gains in overnight and Asian trading. “NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents,” the AI chipmaker said in a press release. The two will work to optimize workflows to maximize Muse’s performance and improve total cost of ownership, and consider additional collaboration opportunities, specifically around Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture. In February, Meta and Nvidia announced a multi-year partnership covering millions of AI GPUs, CPUs and networking technology. They did not reveal the financial details for the deal. Meta’s equity offering follows similar ones by Alphabet (GOOGL) and Intel Corp (INTC) earlier this year – rare moves by the cash-rich companies. During its earnings report last week, Meta announced a new class of nonvoting stock that could ultimately fund acquisitions and other expenses. The so-called Class C stock will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend and will start trading in January 2027. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for META shifted to ‘bullish’ on Tuesday, down from ‘extremely bullish’ the previous day, while sentiment for NVDA remained ‘bullish.’ Trader views on Meta’s offering were mixed and several were holding off for quarterly reports from hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN) later this week to form a position on the stock. Micron (MU) stock rose 1% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday, while Seoul shares of SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics gained 5.6% and 4%, respectively, on Tuesday. South Korea’s Kospi was up 3% at the time of writing. Earlier, the Korea Exchange triggered a “sidecar,” a brief pause in program trading that kicks in when futures move sharply. The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X ETF (KORU) rose 2.8% in overnight trading. The company reported a net loss of $80.7 billion, largely driven by a $72.4 billion accounting charge related to convertible notes. However, Anthropic’s long-term purchase commitments, which flow through to cloud and AI infrastructure providers, caught investors’ attention. The AI company would spend $450 billion in cloud computing agreements over the next seven to ten years, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing the filing. It plans to spend $111 billion on Google cloud computing contracts, $110 billion with Amazon Web Services, and $31 billion on Microsoft, “regardless of actual usage.” Anthropic will also spend up to $86 billion renting Nvidia chips from smaller AI cloud providers Nscale and Lambda through 2033 and 2034, respectively, in addition to other cloud deals, the Journal reported. Anthropic’s financials drew broadly positive comments from analysts and investors, with some praising its pace of growth and deep customer spread. Anthropic will go public on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT," according to the S-1. The company reportedly plans to list its shares in the week of Nov. 16, the Journal reported separately, citing people familiar with the matter. The Federal Reserve is set to meet for its October policy decision on Tuesday, with markets overwhelmingly expecting the central bank to hold rates steady after a 25-basis-point hike at its previous meeting. Morgan Stanley’s chief U.S. economist Michael Gapen agrees with the market, saying that while the Fed will hold rates in October, markets should still expect the policy rate to rise later. In an interview with CNBC, Gapen said that even if the Fed holds rates steady this month, “the Fed's (not) out of the water by any means,” adding that he doesn’t “think they (the Fed) think that” either. Gapen believes the Fed will cite a wait-and-see approach, saying it will watch underlying trends to assess where policy may ultimately go. “So I think that's the balance. They stay on hold,” but with the expectation of policy rates going higher in the future. According to data from the CME FedWatch tool, markets are placing the odds of a ‘Hold’ decision at 88.9%, significantly up from 35.8% a month ago. Meanwhile, the probability of a rate hike of up to 50 bps is 81.6%, according to the website. Gapen thinks the central bank could argue that it will choose how to validate the market’s financial conditions that are tightening. He said, “One argument against going at successive meetings would be the risk of causing too much tightening in financial conditions.” However, he added that there are risks to whichever way the Fed goes, but it would likely take a “more gradual pace.” The economist agreed that the war in the Middle East and rising oil prices would pose a risk to inflation, adding that Morgan Stanley is “factoring some of it into our inflation forecast next year” and that the Federal Open Market Committee will likely consider it as well. The bigger question is whether the central bank can afford to hike benchmark interest rates every other meeting and assess data as it comes, adding that energy markets will likely dictate that course. “I think it's right to think the economy can handle 75 to 100 basis points in total hikes without, without, say, a tremendous amount of concern,” about impact on yields, Gapen said, but cautioned that if the Fed needs to do six or seven total hikes to get back to 2023 levels, then it could cause some concerns. (SPCX) have gained nearly 10% from their IPO offer price, but Bernstein SocGen Group sees room for a much bigger rally — even without assuming a Tesla merger or SpaceX reaching its full revenue ambitions. SPCX shares slipped about 0.4% on Monday, leaving them 9% above their $135 IPO offer price. The research firm raised its price target to $268 from $248, implying an 82% upside from current levels, and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating. “We raise our SpaceX outlook primarily on terrestrial AI build plans. We believe the case for a multi-trillion dollar valuation rests on success of orbital data centers,” the firm said. Bernstein said computing infrastructure on Earth adds materially to SpaceX’s revenue outlook, while its enterprise and government connectivity business also appears to be outperforming. The firm now forecasts $424 billion in full-year 2028 revenue. That remains below SpaceX’s ambition to reach an annualized revenue pace of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, although Bernstein raised its estimate. The company’s goal refers to its revenue pace exiting 2027, rather than total sales during that year. “And, as we have said, you do not need to go all the way to the company’s plan to make SpaceX attractive,” the firm said. Bernstein also noted that SpaceX is planning its first orbital data-center launches in late 2027, with operations beginning in mid-2028. Flight 15 is expected within weeks, with SpaceX planning to catch both the booster and the ship. Bernstein said the heat shield’s performance on Flight 14 could set up the first Starship reuse on Flight 16. “Reusability is key to making orbital data centers successful,” the firm said. Bernstein sees SpaceX’s terrestrial computing capacity reaching 13 gigawatts by the end of 2027 — five gigawatts above its previous forecast — before climbing to 20 gigawatts in 2028. This would mark a sharp jump from the 1.7 gigawatts SpaceX reported at the end of September. On the recent earnings call, Musk said he was confident the company could add 10 gigawatts in 2027, on top of the 2.5 gigawatts to 3 gigawatts expected online by the end of this year. Additionally, Bernstein said the company’s comments pointed to compute prices above the $30 to $50 per watt level seen in recent deals. The firm raised its pricing assumptions but left them below the company’s expectations, leaving room for further gains. “If the company achieves its pricing expectations, there could be more upside, both for terrestrial and orbital,” Bernstein said. Bernstein estimates capex of about $35 billion per gigawatt as SpaceX expands capacity. The company’s earnings call underscored the scale of the spending. CFO Bret Johnsen said Q3 capex totaled $19.6 billion and forecast another $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter. The company also pointed to strong returns on the new infrastructure. “At current pricing, new compute deployments are generating a payback of less than a year,” Johnsen said. SpaceX’s superintelligence segment generated $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, making it the company’s largest revenue segment. Bernstein’s model includes neither a potential Tesla merger nor a reported telecom-tower deal. “Elon talked of a possible Tesla merger and SpaceX is reportedly discussing a telco tower deal,” the firm said. “We make no assumptions on either here.” Separately, ARK Investment Management said that combining the companies could allow Tesla’s potential robotaxi cash generation to help fund SpaceX’s expansion. Its no-premium share-swap scenario projected a 3.8-fold increase in returns for Tesla shareholders and a 7.2-fold increase in incremental returns for SpaceX investors. Musk, however, has cautioned that a transaction remains uncertain. Independent board committees, excluding him because of his conflict of interest, have not agreed on terms. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said. title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth - NVIDIA Newsroom
content:
NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents. Meta’s Muse models and agents, which leverage NVIDIA’s infrastructure, have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Meta and NVIDIA intend to further deepen their collaboration by partnering on optimizations across workflows to maximize performance and improve total cost of ownership. Meta and NVIDIA will also consider additional collaboration opportunities with NVIDIA on its NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, including NVIDIA OpenShell™ for safe deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. This announcement reinforces Meta and NVIDIA’s strong long-term partnership to support Meta’s AI infrastructure ambitions. Meta intends to expand the deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs for next-generation AI agents to deliver maximum performance per watt. Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ Ethernet networking and BlueField-4® to support network efficiency and throughput. In addition, NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering. “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents. NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions.” “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We’re excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people,” said Mark Zuckerberg, founder and CEO of Meta. About NVIDIA

title: Nvidia, Chipmakers Face Higher Costs? TSMC Reportedly Plans Up To 20% Price Hike For Advanced Chip Packaging - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) is preparing to raise prices for its advanced packaging process by 10%-20% as surging demand for AI chips strains production capacity, Taiwan’s China Times reported on Tuesday, citing supply-chain sources. If it goes through with the plan, it would raise costs for several chip firms, including Nvidia Corp (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). The move could also put further pressure on the prices of Apple’s (AAPL) iPhones and MacBooks, which have already seen price increases amid rising memory chip costs. TSMC is considering raising prices for CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate), its advanced packaging technology that integrates chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) into a single package. The report says the potential hike is being considered as demand for advanced packaging expands beyond GPUs to server CPUs and custom AI chips or ASICs, leading to capacity constraints. TSMC is continuing to ramp up its advanced packaging operations to meet demand, with monthly CoWoS capacity expected to exceed 130,000 units in 2026 and 200,000 units next year, China Times reported. TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker, making advanced chips that power everything from AI data centers to smartphones. Its major customers also include Broadcom, Qualcomm and MediaTek. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment was ‘bullish’ for NVDA and AMD, and ‘bearish’ for TSM. TSM stock hit a record high on Oct. 5 but has since been caught up in the selloff in AI-linked stocks amid renewed concerns about the sustainability and returns of massive AI investments. Shares remain 40.5% up year to date. NVDA has declined about 11% from its record close on Oct. 6, but it has been up 16% year-to-date. “$CRWV $NVDA $TSM Ignore the noise from Musk. He's scared,” said a trader, referring to the SpaceX CEO’s bearish comments on the neocloud sector, which pressured several cloud and AI-linked stocks on Monday. Musk had already announced in August, during the company's first earnings conference call, that SpaceX would use Nvidia chips exclusively moving forward. At that time, he said Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture was the best on the market and that SpaceX greatly valued its partnership with Nvidia. Meanwhile, he expected the company's end-of-2027 cumulative computing capacity to be closer to 10 gigawatts than 5 gigawatts. That was a strong indication that SpaceX could triple its AI spending in 2027. However, Musk shocked investors during the company's recent Q3 conference call when he projected that SpaceX would have up to 3 gigawatts of computing capacity by the end of 2026 and is expecting to add an incremental 10 gigawatts of compute power in 2027. However, he said the goal was to add 20 additional gigawatts and that there was a "non-zero possibility" of this happening. title: Nvidia NVDA Stock Rebounds on Chip Sentiment Improving but Data-Centre Risks Remain - FXLeaders
content: Nvidia stock rebounded from $210 as semiconductor sentiment improved, but data-centre power shortages, expensive financing, manufacturing constraints and growing competition raise questions about whether infrastructure spending can sustain demand for advanced processors. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) shares recovered above $215 after touching $210 last Friday, regaining some ground following a retreat from a record above $243 earlier this month. The rebound reflects renewed buying interest across the semiconductor sector, supported by expectations that memory shortages and higher prices could persist through 2027. However, the recovery comes as investors increasingly question the financial returns from expanding computing infrastructure. Rising borrowing costs, expensive equipment and electricity constraints are complicating the expansion plans of major technology companies. Nvidia remains a leading supplier of advanced processors, but its growth increasingly depends on customers having the financial resources, electricity and infrastructure required to deploy the hardware they purchase. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) is reportedly purchasing billions of dollars in Nvidia hardware, yet some server racks are sitting in warehouses because data centres lack sufficient electricity to operate them, according to Business Insider. Internal emails reportedly indicated that Amazon expected to receive $5 billion in Nvidia server systems in August, followed by another $3 billion monthly. The company also introduced an Early Rack Receipt programme, allowing it to secure equipment before facilities are ready for deployment. Previously, Amazon generally waited until hardware reached its data centres before taking ownership. The revised arrangement helps secure scarce equipment but also exposes the company to storage costs and delays between delivery and commercial use. For Nvidia, this highlights a potential weakness in the infrastructure expansion cycle. Strong orders may support near-term demand, but delayed deployments could postpone returns for customers and influence future purchasing decisions. If electricity shortages persist, technology companies may reconsider the timing and scale of new projects, particularly as infrastructure costs rise. Expectations for higher memory prices have provided some support to semiconductor shares. Dell CEO Michael Dell reportedly warned that memory shortages could worsen in 2027, while analysts at Mizuho and KeyBanc have highlighted the potential for NAND flash prices to increase as demand for computing infrastructure expands. Higher memory prices could benefit manufacturers across the supply chain, but they also increase the cost of building and operating data centres. For Nvidia, the key question is whether customers can maintain their investment plans while absorbing rising expenses for processors, memory, electricity and construction. NVIDIA shares lost momentum early in September after failing to break decisively above the $236 resistance zone, with the rejection sending the stock back below $210 but we have seen a decent rebound recently. Shares have climbed above $233 today as investors responded positively to expanding infrastructure partnerships and CEO projections, but buyers are not able to sustain the rally above $243 and we saw dive to $210 again last week but we’re seeing some improvement this week. ASML reported record third-quarter sales of €11.7 billion but warned that planned semiconductor manufacturing capacity in 2027 and 2028 might not fully meet anticipated demand. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion and narrowed its 2026 sales guidance to €44 billion–€45 billion. Despite these figures, its U.S.-listed shares reportedly fell approximately 4%, adding pressure to Nvidia and AMD. Manufacturing constraints could support semiconductor pricing, but they may also delay the equipment needed to expand production. This creates a difficult balance for the industry: demand remains strong, yet supply limitations could restrict growth. Financing concerns have intensified following heavy selling in CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV). Yields on its $1.25 billion bond issue due in 2032 reportedly reached 15% before closing near 14.5%, signalling substantial investor concern about credit risk. Such borrowing costs raise questions about the sustainability of debt-financed data-centre expansion. If infrastructure operators face increasingly expensive financing, some projects could be delayed or scaled back, weakening future demand for Nvidia processors. Reported financing discussions involving major technology companies further illustrate the substantial capital required to sustain the industry’s expansion. Microsoft’s Maia 300 processor adds another competitive risk. The chip reportedly targets 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, while a 96-accelerator configuration is designed to deliver up to seven times the rack-scale throughput of its predecessor. Custom silicon could help cloud providers improve efficiency and reduce dependence on external suppliers for selected workloads. Nvidia’s established software ecosystem and broad customer base remain important advantages, but increasingly capable alternatives could eventually pressure its pricing power and market share in specific applications. Questions about OpenAI’s revenue have renewed scrutiny of technology-sector spending assumptions. Its annualised revenue run rate was reportedly around $50 billion at the end of September, below the widely circulated $68 billion figure, which reportedly included revenue generated by partners. The distinction matters because investors need evidence that the commercial demand supporting infrastructure investment can justify its enormous costs. If revenue growth fails to keep pace with spending, technology companies could face pressure to reduce capital expenditure, potentially affecting future processor orders. Nvidia’s rebound above $215 provides some relief after the retreat from $243, but the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed selling. The ability to sustain gains will depend partly on whether major customers can overcome electricity constraints, secure financing and generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure investments. For now, memory shortages and continued demand for advanced processors support the bullish case. However, rising financing costs, manufacturing bottlenecks and competition from custom chips create significant risks. Nvidia’s long-term growth prospects remain substantial, but the sustainability of its rally increasingly depends on whether customers can turn expensive computing infrastructure into profitable businesses.

title: Jensen Huang Says Nvidia's Next-Gen Vera Rubin Chips Will Generate $40 Billion in Revenue per Gigawatt, Up From $25 Billion for Grace Blackwell. What That Means for NVDA's Growth Runway. - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia says each gigawatt of AI capacity is now worth 60% more to it with Vera Rubin, and that could extend its growth runway even if customers don't add more power. Nvidia (NVDA +0.90%) has already made an incredible amount of money selling the powerful chips that drive artificial intelligence (AI). But CEO Jensen Huang believes the company's biggest opportunities are still ahead, and Nvidia's newest technology could help him prove it. The chipmaker's next-generation Vera Rubin architecture is designed to deliver substantially more computing power from the same amount of electricity. That's important for cloud companies that are racing to build AI data centers, where access to power has become a major constraint. But there's another benefit for Nvidia shareholders. Vera Rubin could generate 60% more revenue per gigawatt of computing capacity than its predecessor. And that helps explain why Huang is so confident about Nvidia's growth runway. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images. Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell graphics processing units (GPUs) have been enormously successful with hyperscalers and smaller cloud providers building artificial intelligence computing capacity. But Nvidia isn't simply selling faster GPUs anymore. Its Vera Rubin platform combines Rubin GPUs, Vera central processing units (CPUs), high-speed NVLink connections, networking equipment, and software into a complete AI computing system. NVLink enables processors to communicate and share memory access more efficiently, helping customers complete more computing work without a corresponding increase in electricity consumption. During Nvidia's fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings call in August, Huang explained how that expanding platform translates into a bigger revenue opportunity. "In the case of Hopper, we were at about $18 billion per gigawatt. For Grace Blackwell, we're at about $25 billion per gigawatt. And for Vera Rubin, it's about $40 billion per gigawatt," he said. "And the productivity is X-factors increase in each generation." That's a 60% increase over Blackwell, even if customers don't build any additional power capacity. And the technology is already moving into the market. Nvidia says Vera Rubin has entered production shipments, with purchase orders from major hyperscalers, AI cloud providers, and equipment manufacturers. Huang predicted last year that AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030, and he reiterated that forecast in September. He's also expecting Nvidia to sell twice as many chips in 2027 as in 2026, according to comments he made to reporters in Scotland on Sept. 17. That doesn't necessarily mean Nvidia's revenue will double. Chip volumes and revenue are different measurements, and the $40 billion-per-gigawatt figure represents a potential sales opportunity rather than guaranteed orders. But the underlying business is already growing at an extraordinary pace. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in revenue for its fiscal second quarter, which ended July 26, up 106% from a year earlier. Data center revenue alone reached $89 billion. Vera Rubin gives Nvidia another way to increase revenue beyond simply selling more GPUs. If customers continue to expand their AI capacity while spending more per gigawatt on Nvidia technology, the company's growth runway could be considerably longer than its already massive size suggests. NVLink enables processors to communicate and share memory access more efficiently, helping customers complete more computing work without a corresponding increase in electricity consumption. During Nvidia's fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings call in August, Huang explained how that expanding platform translates into a bigger revenue opportunity. "In the case of Hopper, we were at about $18 billion per gigawatt. For Grace Blackwell, we're at about $25 billion per gigawatt. And for Vera Rubin, it's about $40 billion per gigawatt," he said. "And the productivity is X-factors increase in each generation." That's a 60% increase over Blackwell, even if customers don't build any additional power capacity. And the technology is already moving into the market. Nvidia says Vera Rubin has entered production shipments, with purchase orders from major hyperscalers, AI cloud providers, and equipment manufacturers. Huang predicted last year that AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030, and he reiterated that forecast in September. He's also expecting Nvidia to sell twice as many chips in 2027 as in 2026, according to comments he made to reporters in Scotland on Sept. 17. That doesn't necessarily mean Nvidia's revenue will double. Chip volumes and revenue are different measurements, and the $40 billion-per-gigawatt figure represents a potential sales opportunity rather than guaranteed orders. But the underlying business is already growing at an extraordinary pace. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in revenue for its fiscal second quarter, which ended July 26, up 106% from a year earlier. Data center revenue alone reached $89 billion. Vera Rubin gives Nvidia another way to increase revenue beyond simply selling more GPUs. If customers continue to expand their AI capacity while spending more per gigawatt on Nvidia technology, the company's growth runway could be considerably longer than its already massive size suggests. title: Questions Arise Over Neoclouds’ Operational Stability, Testing NVIDIA’s (NVDA.US) Role as an AI Financier - 富途牛牛
content: NVIDIA (NVDA.US) stated that, as credit markets tighten for its major partners, the company's role as a global financier of AI infrastructure is facing its first major stress test. After launching relevant chips in the early stages of generative AI, NVIDIA began leveraging its financial strength to provide funding support to AI model developers, data center companies, and several so‑called neoclouds (new cloud service providers). CEO Jensen Huang's strategy, in addition to building cutting‑edge technology, also involves offering customers investment and loan assistance to promote broader adoption of the systems. The arrangements include leveraging NVIDIA's investment-grade credit rating to provide guarantees for OpenAI's large-scale projects, enabling the related construction to secure financing at lower interest rates. As of the most recent quarterly financial filing in July, NVIDIA has entered into off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements or guarantees involving neoclouds totaling $36 billion, and it has also provided up to $105 billion in guarantees for chips, land, and electricity related to OpenAI's plan to build a 10-gigawatt data center in Ohio. The company has also signed $20 billion in future data center leases, which it will subsequently transfer to third parties. Under most transactions, NVIDIA is only liable for payment if the project participants default. David Trainer, founder and CEO of the financial research firm New Constructs, stated that if computing power demand fails to meet the market's extremely high expectations, problems will arise. Market conditions may test NVIDIA's resilience. In NVIDIA's portfolio, neoclouds such as CoreWeave (CRWV.US), Nebius (NBIS.US), and IREN (IREN.US)—all of which continue to burn cash—have all seen their stock prices plunge by at least 30% this month. Among them, the largest, CoreWeave, has seen its credit default swap spread rise above 11%, reflecting that investors must pay higher premiums to guard against default. Other neoclouds backed by NVIDIA are also facing challenges. The company is an investor in Firmus, an Australian AI cloud provider, which abruptly withdrew its IPO plans this month; UK-based Nscale and SB Energy, which is supported by SoftBank, also filed to list in the U.S. in September, but there has been no update on their progress for several weeks. Last week, Jensen Huang reiterated his confidence in the market, telling CNBC that demand for neoclouds is "extremely strong." During an interview with CNBC at the GTC conference in Berlin, Huang noted that what's currently lacking is working capital to support growth, as surging demand across multiple AI sectors has led to a shortage of available capital. NVIDIA has invested in dozens of companies, including substantial stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic. As of the second quarter, its investment portfolio was valued at $99 billion. Investors told CNBC that the market is watching how NVIDIA will use its cash and its $5 trillion market capitalization to deliver more chips to customers, as well as how much risk the company is willing to take. Brian Stutland, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said that market volatility reflects investors' concerns about business stability. He noted that CoreWeave and other neoclouds enter into long-term contracts; while their earnings reports appear promising, the market is focused on whether these contracts can remain stable. title: Is Nvidia Stock Cheaper Now That Its Multiple Has Fallen? - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Many investors evaluate NVIDIA (NVDA) the way they evaluate any stock: the lower the price-to-earnings multiple, the cheaper the stock. That multiple, what investors pay for each dollar of profit, stood at 101.3 for Nvidia in mid-2023. Today it is 26.5. Does a multiple that has fallen this far mean you are getting a cheaper stock? Nvidia’s share price rose 398.7% from mid-2023 to October 23, 2026, excluding dividends. A single share now costs far more than it did, while each dollar of profit behind it costs far less. Over the same three years, the price went up and the multiple went down. Nvidia’s profit over the latest twelve months reached $193 billion, compared with $10.3 billion in the twelve months to mid-2023. That is 18.7 times as much profit in three years. The table below shows how profit and the multiple moved year by year. Net income is the reported total for the twelve months ending on the date shown. Change in a year compares that net income to the twelve months prior. Each price-to-earnings multiple divides the market value at the calendar quarter end paired with those twelve months by the net income for those twelve months; the final row uses the share price of Oct 23, 2026. Nvidia generates its sales mostly from one business: the Compute & Networking segment made up 89.6% of revenue in fiscal 2026. On the August 26, 2026 call, management said a surge in AI demand is driving a global infrastructure buildout, and that sustained strength in Blackwell drove sales to hyperscale customers. Not in the way the rule suggests. A better question is what investors were paying for when the multiple was high. Nvidia’s multiple peaked at 143.1 in early 2023, when twelve-month profit had dipped to about $4.8 billion. Profit today is about 40 times that. Investors paid the most for each dollar of profit when there was far less of it because they expected it to grow, and it did. Today, a buyer pays less for each dollar of profit than a buyer did three years ago. That earlier buyer was paying for growth that has since happened. The lower multiple partly reflects growth that has already arrived, so it is not by itself a discount. This follows the usual curve for a fast grower: the multiple is highest while the profit is still expected, and lower once it is here. Nvidia’s profit is still growing fast, and it is expanding faster than it did a year earlier. Profit rose 122.7% in the latest twelve months, compared with 63.4% the year before. Profit also grew faster than sales, which rose 83.4%. Nvidia’s multiple today sits above the S&P 500’s 22.9. When Nvidia reports in November 2026, the figure to watch is whether profit keeps growing near the latest year’s pace. title: GOOGL's $250B AI Chip Opportunity Takes Aim At NVDA — Beth Kindig Says Google Is Going After ‘One Of The Most Profitable Hardware Businesses’ - TradingView
content: Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) could be positioning its artificial intelligence chips as a serious challenge to Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), with third-party Tensor Processing Unit sales potentially becoming a major new revenue stream, according to IO Fund analyst Beth Kindig. In a note on Friday, Kindig said Google's advantage may not come from simply building a faster accelerator, but from attacking the economics of AI infrastructure, particularly the cost of running increasingly expensive AI workloads. She said Google’s AI story is about to change “not from advancements in AI software, but by going after one of the most profitable hardware businesses the tech industry has ever seen.” Alphabet’s Class A shares closed 1% lower in Friday’s regular trading session, while Nvidia shares fell about 0.6%. Kindig Points To Google Targeting AI's Biggest Cost Problem With TPU Strategy Kindig says the AI accelerator market is entering a new phase as Google moves its merchant TPU strategy from announcement toward commercial execution. Google recognized its first TPU-related revenue from third-party customers in the second quarter. The analyst noted that the focus is increasingly on cost per token now, as massive AI infrastructure spending puts pressure on Big Tech's free cash flow. Google's latest TPU 8t and 8i systems are designed to improve performance per dollar compared with the previous-generation Ironwood TPU. Kindig says TPU 8i can deliver up to an 80% improvement in performance per dollar, particularly for low-latency inference workloads, while TPU 8t offers up to 2.7 times better performance per dollar for training. The result could allow customers to process substantially more AI workloads for the same infrastructure spending. “Google’s greatest competitive advantage may not be building a faster chip than Nvidia, but rather in building AI infrastructure at a lower cost,” she added. Kindig believes that the bigger opportunity for Google could come from the company selling TPUs directly to third-party customers rather than exclusively deploying them through Google Cloud. She added that this would create a second revenue stream for Google while shifting much of the upfront infrastructure burden toward customers, including data centers, power, cooling and hardware. Anthropic is already expected to deploy a gigawatt of Ironwood TPUs in 2026, followed by 5GW of TPU 8i in 2027 and another 10GW in 2028, according to Broadcom's update cited by Kindig, who believes that this would create a significant revenue stream for the company. At the high end, that would represent a staggering acceleration for Google's chip business, potentially reaching the current run rate of its Search business in just a few years, the analyst noted. Google Could Challenge Nvidia Beyond Inference, Says Kindig Google's threat to Nvidia also extends beyond inference. Kindig highlights TPU 8t's ability to scale to a 9,600-chip superpod with 2PB of shared HBM and 121 exaflops of FP4 compute. Google's Virgo Network fabric can then connect 14 such superpods, creating a domain capable of supporting 134,400 TPUs. The scale could become particularly important if Nvidia encounters further delays with its next-generation systems, potentially giving Google additional room to gain accelerator share, she added. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Alphabet trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing. GOOGL stock is up 2% year-to-date, while NVDA stock is up 13%.
